The city is divided into three parts: the Inner City is home of the rich, the Industrial Quarter is home of all the workshops and marketplaces, the Shanty Quarter is home to the destitute and criminal-minded.

entries.name: Helixia
entries.content: Helixia is the capital of the Antanath.

entries.name: Helpulus
entries.content: Helpulus is a naturalist shrine-city within southeastern Dragoc. It is the shrine of life and nature.

entries.name: House of Darkness
entries.content:
The House of Darkness is the administrative center of the Mori Templa Mellon clan, their "parliament", basically. From the outside, it looks like some kind of palace, shrine or hostel - or some interesting hybrid of the three. In truth, it is a bit of all of them, in addition to being their administrative center: this is where their dark witches and dark priests go to rest and force the slaves to pamper them. Usually, only women are allowed to enter, unless the male in question has a good reason to go inside.

Aside from the living quarters, the most important parts of the building are the council room - where the clan's leader sits to have a council with the council - and the throne room, where the clan's leader calls herself a "queen", despite having no crown.

entries.name: House of Light
entries.content: The House of Light is the residence of Froturn's royla family, located in Yanus. Despite being one building, the air is always clean, as there are many windows, vents, artificial cannals and green space.

entries.name: Kelu e Taure
entries.content: Kelu e Taure is an Artaburran border town near the Artaburran border with Dragoc. As such, it is inhabited by Half-Elves and Wood Elves alike. This is a town with economic functions, focused on trade.

entries.name: Killer Life
entries.content: The Killer Life is a Keldornish inn and tradehouse located in Magnus Nex Urbs. It is a building with looks that the undead deem attractive. It is a black market (if such a thing can even exist in Keldorn, where the laws are extremely lax), where one can buy pretty much anything. They also serve drinks and have rentable rooms for lodging. The building is own by a ghost, who controls 20 zombies to fufill the needs of his clients. All business transactions take place on the bottom floor, which must be communicated with the owner, as the zombies have no consciousness of their own.

entries.name: Lamrion
entries.content: The Forest of Hate, also known as Lamrion is a location within the Kingdom of Etrand, stated to be near the town of Talon. It is reputed to be a hideout of various undead beings that prey on the living after sunset, but so far no one has been able to prove the rumour to be anything more than a superstition - or rather, no one lived to tell the tale of what they encountered in Lamrion.

entries.name: Library of Darkness
entries.content: The Library of Darkness is effectively the sanctuary of dark knowledge located within Atrum Libri, where just about all books about black magic can be found here - or so they claim. The books and booklets needed to master the basics are found on the first floor; the second floor stores studying material for those with more advanced skills; the third floor is the one where most powerful dark spells are stored, where they only let in the most high-ranked dark wizards to enter, as the terrible powers contained within them would only lead to a weaker apprentice accidentally self-destructing.

entries.name: Lynsárne
entries.content: Lynsárne, a village in Northwestern Etrand, was founded in 7 AEKE by High Elven settlers invited by King Corlagon I. Initially established for spreading the new state religion, the settlers, including a few farmers, formed villages like Lynsárne. Enjoying privileges like yeoman status without mandatory military service, the village evolved over centuries. It later attracted human and halfling immigrants, diminishing the High Elven presence. Despite this, Lynsárne maintains a unique identity with a blend of human and Elven influences in its architecture and culture. The human majority still celebrates Elven festivals, preserving a distinct character.

entries.name: Magnus Nex Urbs
entries.content: Magnus Nex Urbs is the capital city of the Republic of Keldorn.

entries.name: Minosa
entries.content: Minosa is a Naturalist shrine-city within the northwestern part of Dragoc, as well as the capital city of the kingdom

entries.name: Needle Rock
entries.content: The Needle Rock is a mountain located not so far from the Gray Mountains, surrouneded by a forest. It is a well-known landmark, and as such, multiple historical monarchs have met the Kings of Etrand at this place. There were occasions when they put down the tents for weeks and celebrated their old friendships or new agreements with extravagrant feasts - but this is all history. Nowadays, it is mostly travellers who briefly look at the Needle Rock while passing through. Yet, the Needle Rock unflinchingly stands as a reminder to the old times, when the monarchs of the various countries expressed respect for each other via their personal presence.

entries.name: Nex Mucró
entries.content: Nex Mucró is a Keldornish fortified city, the main military center of the undead.

entries.name: Noldó Ranga
entries.content: Noldó Ranga is a small town in Froturn, populated mainly by Halflings.

entries.name: Palace of Holy Kings
entries.content: The Palace of Holy Kings is the residence of the royal family of Etrand, and also serves as a Titanist cathedral, albeit reserved only for nobility and more prestigeous foreigners. It is located within Grandfolk.

entries.name: Qariash Islands
entries.content:
The Qariash Islands in Gabyrian, Cymbierd Islands in Etrancoasti or Cymbair Islands in Etrandish are an archipelago within the Occident, currently under Gabyrian rule. A strategical location for controlling trade between the Occident and the Orient, the island cluster is actually more famously known for being fought over by Etrand and Gabyr in multiple wars.

These islands are mostly uninhabited. Having infertile soil and no natural resources at all whatsoever, the islands house no permanent residents, only temporary residents: dockworkers, military garrisons and travelling merchants.

entries.name: Rodiou
entries.content: Rodiou is a Naturalist shrine-city within the southwestern part of Dragoc. It is the shrine of hunters. During war time, they pray here to get enough strength to win the war. During peace time, they present their sacrifices out of gratefullness to their gods, that the last hunt was a success. Aside from praying, this is also where adults compete with each other in martial contests, such as brawls to exhaustion in an arena-like building. Killing is forbidden, as it is punished by exile. The forest around the shrine also serves as a home for the Wood Elves - they build their houses on top of the trees, so the surroundings of the shrine have grown into city of sorts.

entries.name: Scaurwél
entries.content: Scaurwél - also known as Scaarghél - is an island under Etrandish rule, populated by less than five thousand people, almost exclusively Etrandish-speaking Humans following the Church of Titanius. While the island is nominally under Etrandish rule, in reality, due to their isolation and lack of importance, the islanders are largely left to their own devices, with de facto political power being in hands of the church, and the island's de facto governor being the local abbot.

entries.name: Stélhelm
entries.content: Sélhelm or Steelhelm - also known by its Dwarven name Shtíl Kålåm - is a city within Northern Etrand and arguably the most ancient city within Etrand proper, if we disregard the various Dwarven cities. Stélhelm is also the capital of the Margraviate of Steelhelm.

entries.name: Talon
entries.content: Talon is a village or small town in Southern Etrand, the second largest settlement in Southern Etrand next to Copperport. The town is separated in two by the River Golea.

entries.name: The Black Finger
entries.content: The Black Finger is a very much ruined tavern for very much ruined people, located within Grandfolk. They only serve beer and bread, there are barely five tables each with two chairs (except the left one, which has only one). The owner is Balmari, a one-eyed man who is always grumpy but never says a word - he just grumbles when he doesn't like something. Strangely, when he does this, all the frequenters and haunters immediately go silent.

entries.name: The Bloody Bear Inn
entries.content: The Bloody Bear Inn is an Etrandish inn, located in the Harbour District of Copperport. The bar at the ground floor has twelve chairs - there are also ten tables, with each having four seats. On the first and second floors are the rentable rooms.

entries.name: The Blue Dragon Inn
entries.content: The Blue Dragon Inn is Helixia's one and only inn. Many Halflings come here on a daily basis to eat, drink and rest. The ground floor's bar has 10 seats, there are also 6 tables, each with 4 seats. The one and only floor has the rentable rooms.

entries.name: The Broken Triangle Tavern
entries.content: The Broken Triangle Tavern is a Froturnish tavern located in Edhel Yára. The bar at the ground floor has 14 seats, while there are 8 tables, each with 4 seats. As it is a tavern - not an inn - there are no rentable rooms.

entries.name: The Cut-Down Candle Inn
entries.content: The Cut-Down Candle Inn is an Etrandish inn, located in Etrocast. The ground floor has twelve tables, each with six seats, while the bar has eight chairs. The first and only floor is where the rentable rooms are.

entries.name: The Dead Man
entries.content: The Dead Man is a Keldornish tavern located in Atrum Libri. A rather scary, dark, decrepit and seedy-looking place, it is the favourite of the undead. The bartender is Gorphon Hamaridjak, a werewolf who growls at everyone who enters, but most people have already gotten used to it. The undead mostly use this place to hold "banquets" - of course, they also sit down to tell each other about their latest vilainous acts and laugh together. Those Necromancers and Death Knights who are still mortals are served beer, bread and mushrooms, while Vampires and Theriantropes (such as Werewolves) are served blood.

entries.name: The Drunken Raven Inn
entries.content: The Drunken Raven Inn is a "inn" in the Shanty Quarter of Grandfolk - at least on paper, in reality, it is more of a black market, a racket. When something is too expensive for you, or you can't find it anywhere, this is where you look for it - assuming that you have knowledge of that secondary tavern within the building, where the frequenters go into the room behind the bar. Casper, the bartender does not look upon unknown pryers with fondness. It goes without saying that this place is the favourite stamping ground of the local thieves.

entries.name: The Earth-Running Snake Inn
entries.content: The Earth-Running Snake Inn is an Etrandish inn, located in the Inner City of Copperport. The bar at the ground floor has ten chairs - there are also eight tables, with each having six seats. On the first and second floors are the rentable rooms.

entries.name: The Fiery Steed Inn
entries.content: The Fiery Steed Inn is an Etrandish inn located in Zorod Koldó im Neuna. The bar at the ground floor has twelve chairs attached, along with six tables, each with six chairs. The first and only floor is where all the rentable rooms are.

entries.name: The Finger of Fire Inn
entries.content: The Finger of Fire Inn is a Froturnish inn located in Yanus. The bar at the ground floor has 12 seats, while there are 6 tables, each with 6 seats. The rentable rooms are on the first floor. The local speciality is the Snow-White Sugary.

entries.name: The Fur-Hiding Bear Gathering Place
entries.content:
The Fur-Hiding Bear "Gathering Place" is a building in Zorod Koldo im Neuna, functioning as a de facto tavern, where they mostly only serve beer, water and bread. There are twelve chairs at the bar, there are ten tables, each with four chairs.

Humans seldom - if ever - frequent this place. While they aren't legally barred from entering per se, they aren't looked upon fondly: this place is effectively a sanctuary, a gathering place for the various racial minorities (that is, non-Humans) of the kingdom - which is ironic, since Humans themselves as a minority in the city of Zorod Koldo im Neuna, populated overwhelmingly by Dwarves and Gnomes.

entries.name: The Hall of Blacksmiths
entries.content: The Hall of Blacksmiths is an Etrandish institution, located within Zorod Koldó im Neuna. It is the center of the local Dwarven population in the city, and among the only places where Dwarven Steel and Living Metal can be safely experimented with. It is also the place where the statues of the most prominent blacksmiths are put. Additionally, within the cellars, they plan out the trade routes.

entries.name: The Lava Towers of the Zorods
keys: the lava towers of the zorods
The Lava Towers of the Zorods
entries.content: Zorod Koldo im Neuna and Zorod Naugi im Pkhaur both contain so-called lava towers (both cities have 12 towers each), which prevent the eruption of volcanoes right underneath those two cities that were built straight over active volcanoes. In each of these towers, there a so-called "ice crystal", which projects an invisible protective layer upon the surface of the lava. When the lava touches that boundary, it turns into stone, and falls back into the lava. A quite big problem, is that this only applies to lava - heat still goes up, and man can fall inside (potentially freezing before falling into the lava). To maintain this protective shield around a city, there needs to be 12 towers - if one malfunctions, the whole thing goes under, therefore only specialists are allowed to enter these towers.
entries.comment: The Lava Towers of the Zorods

entries.name: The Left Hand of Salashi
entries.content: The Left Hand of Salashi is a tavern and restaurant in Grandfolk that was founded by and is led by Frensus Salashi. The Left Hand of Salashi is a very well-furnished place - one of the cosiest, if not the cosiest resort in all of Grandfolk out of all the premises that ordinary citizens can even dream of approaching -, which operates as a restaurant during day time and as a "nightclub" (with all the music and dancing) during night time. Food, drink, female dancers are all here for both travellers and local frequent visitors. The owner is Frensus Salashi, whose left hand is missing under his wrist, yet he is able to do everything perfectly and is as adept as a person with 3 hands - hence the name "The Left Hand of Salashi".

entries.name: The Let-Down Harpoon Tavern
entries.content: The Let-Down Harpoon Tavern is an Etrancoasti tavern, located in the Harbour District of Yrvháven. The bar has twelve chairs. There are fourteen tables, each with eight seats. Since it is a tavern - not an inn - there are no rentable rooms!

entries.name: The Picked-Up Anchor Tavern
entries.content: The Picked-Up Anchor Tavern is an Etrancoasti tavern, located in the Harbour District of Wáterbúrcht. The bar has twelve chairs. There are eight tables, each with four seats. Since it is a tavern - not an inn - there are no rentable rooms!

entries.name: The Poisoned Sword Inn
entries.content:
The Poisoned Sword Inn is a typical underground inn located on the domain of the Dhaeraow Loomin clan, where they don't like foreigners, where they happily beat the weak into a pulp. The inside of the building is very divisive, as some consider it beautiful and exotic, while others consider it straight-up distasteful: everything is painted black, and most things are made out of iron. The lighting is done by crystals that emit a blue light.

On the "ground floor" - if we can even call it that (the floor that the entrance directly leads to), the bar has 10 seats, together with 5 tables, each with 4 seats. The bartender is Droku'n de Almidus, a middle-aged Dark Elf, who is quite rude... but if you are angry at him, you could easily find yourself the victim of a poisoned arrow.

entries.name: The Purple Brother Brothel
entries.content: The Purple Brother Brothel is a brothel within the Shanty Quarter of Grandfolk. The building's most notable frequenter and haunter is Cradar the Once-Unclean, an old medicine-man, who earns his daily bread by charging money for using his magic to cure people of the various sexually-transmitted diseases they tend to get from the fine ladies of this establishment - of course, he also provides precautionary measures to prevent said fine ladies from catching such diseases from their clients as well.

entries.name: The Rested Wolf Inn
entries.content: The Rested Wolf Inn is an Etrandish inn located in Dracfold. The bar on the ground floor has 12 seats, there are 14 tables each with 8 chairs. The following three floors contain the rentable rooms.

entries.name: The Rusty Battleaxe Tavern
entries.content: The Rusty Battleaxe Tavern is an Etrancoasti tavern, located in the Inner City of Yrvháven. The bar has eight chairs. There are ten tables, each with six seats. Since it is a tavern - not an inn - there are no rentable rooms!

entries.name: The Rusty Sword Tavern
entries.content: The Rusty Sword Tavern is an Etrancoasti tavern, located in the Inner City of Wáterbúrcht. The bar has twelve chairs. There are eight tables, each with four seats. Since it is a tavern - not an inn - there are no rentable rooms!

entries.name: The Scrawny Oak Inn
entries.content: The Scrawny Oak Inn is an Artaburran inn located in Kelu e Taure. Its name is not a low - it really was built from oak wood. The ground has a bar with twelve seats, additionally with ten tables, each with six seats. The first and second floors contain the rentable rooms.

entries.name: The Sizzling Sun
entries.content: The Sizzling Sun is not an ordinary inn - as it is the headquarters of the very secretive Brotherhood of the Dark Moon, who are trying to keep their very existence a secret. The prices for rooms are very high, while food and drinks are sold at an acceptable price, at a quality better than usual - the local speciality is Zalag's Soup. There are ten tables at the ground floor, each with four seats, while the bar has eight chairs. This building holds a lot of secrets.

entries.name: The Skinned Bear Inn
entries.content: The Skinned Bear Inn is an Etrandish inn. On the ground floor, the bar has 8 chairs, and there are 8 tables, each with 4 chairs. The first and only floor is where the rentable rooms are.

entries.name: The Split Sling Tavern
entries.content: The Split Sling Tavern is a Froturnish tavern located in Noldó Ranga. The bar at the ground floor has 12 seats, while there are 10 tables, each with 8 seats. As it is a tavern - not an inn - there are no rentable rooms.

entries.name: The Sylvan Bow Inn
entries.content: The Sylvan Bow Inn is an Artaburran inn located in Alta Gon. The bar has eight seats. There are also ten tables, each with six seats. The first and second floors have the rentable rooms.

entries.name: The Thrown Javelin Tavern
entries.content: The Thrown Javelin Tavern is a Froturnish tavern located in Wohun. The bar at the ground floor has 8 seats, while there are 5 tables, each with 4 seats. As it is a tavern - not an inn - there are no rentable rooms.

entries.name: The Unforgeable Chainmail Tavern
entries.content: The Unforgeable Chainmail Tavernis an Etrandish tavenr located in Zorod Naugi im Pkhaur. There are 8 seats at the bar, while there are 6 tables, each with 5 chairs. This is a tavern, not an inn - therefore, there are no rentable rooms!

entries.name: The Wounded Lion Inn
entries.content: The Wounded Lion Inn is an Etrandish inn in Talon. On the ground floor, there is a bar with eight chairs, and there are twenty tables, each with six chairs. The first and second floors contain all the rentable rooms. The local speciality is Pumpkin Beer.

entries.name: Valley of Equilibrium
entries.content: The Valley of Equilibrium is a hidden location within Northwestern Etrand. It is a magic nexus.

entries.name: Wáterbúrcht
entries.content: Wáterbúrcht is an Etrancoasti city. It is a port city, located right on the beach. Not just on the beach, but also right next to a river that flows into the sea - however, unlike Yrvháven, Wáterbúrcht isn't separated in two by said river, as the city made the decision to be only one one side of said river.

entries.name: Willem's Tavern
entries.content:
Willem's Tavern is an Artaburran inn, located in Yára Linde. There are ten seats by the bar, and there are six tables, each with four chairs. Given that it is a tavern - not an inn - there are no rentable rooms.

As its name suggests, tt is ran by a human named Willem, who was originally born in Etrancoast, bringing Etrancoasti humour and jokes with himself to the tavern, making the entertainment of the patrons with his jokes his second duty (which are supposedly really good).

entries.name: Wohun
entries.content: Wohun is a fortified city in Central Froturn.

entries.name: Yanus
entries.content: Yanus is the capital city of Froturn, and currently the third largest city in Continental Artograch after Neressa and Grandfolk. Yanus is considered a centre of learning, and is also in many ways, a centre of the Church of Titanius.

entries.name: Yára Linde
entries.content: Yára Linde is a fortified city within the Principality of Artaburro, their main national redoubt.

entries.name: Yrvháven
entries.content: Yrvháven is the capital city of Etrancoast. It is a port city, right next to the sea, separated in two by a river which flows into the sea. A large bridge connects the two parts.

entries.name: Zargonath
entries.content: Zargonath is an mine in Antanath, created as soon as the Halflings began settling the region. It has a large chamber, which consists of multiple excavations and mines. Limestone, gemstone and stalactite mining is very significant to this settlement. Two lanterns are to be found in the smaller canyon in front of the entrance. It took about one year for the halflings to smoothen the walls and ceilings of the corridors accross the entrance.

entries.name: Zorod Koldó im Neuna
entries.content: Zorod Koldó im Neuna is a mountain city inhabited mainly by Dwarves and Gnomes - as well as the representatives of various other races, as this is the de facto administrative center of Etrand's Autonomous Dwarven Region.

entries.name: Zorod Naugi im Pkhaur
entries.content: Zorod Naugi im Pkhaur is a mountain city in Etrand populated overwhelmingly by Dwarves and Gnomes.

entries.name: Aelfwaird of Dracfold
entries.content: Aelfwaird of Dracfold (12 BEKE - 52 AEKE) was the Grand Count of Dracfold between 19 and 53, and the most famous member of the House of Dracfold. He was also Anti-king, and paternal grandfather of King Hengist I of Etrand.

entries.name: Aethling Tondbertling
entries.content: Aethling Tondbertling (722 - 783 AEKE) was an Etrandish the Grand Count of Brevia between 767 and 783 (although he did act a de facto regent for his father between 760 and 767, as his health was declining). He re-established Tondbertid influence in the royal court and made peace with the Cairbré-regime, while at the same time expanding his family's influence in the region.

entries.name: Anastasoula Rasviros
entries.content: Anastasoula Rasviros is an Etrandish Weretiger Magician/Bard.

entries.name: Aran Shéd
entries.content: Aran Shéd is a Dark Elven Magician and a Headhunter.

entries.name: Archbishop Eurenic Bryantling of Grandfolk
entries.content:
Archbishop Eurenic Bryantling (720-795 AEKE) or Crown Prince Eurenic of Etrand was the older brother of King Cairbré I of Etrand, eldest son of King Bryant I of Etrand. He was the heir apparent of King Bryant, but circumstances after Bryant's death ensured Cairbré's ascension to the throne, leading to Eurenic's revolt, which in turn led to the former crown prince being blinded and forced to retire to a monastery. As a member of the Frettinoarian Order.

He eventually reconciled with Cairbré, which led to him becoming the Archbishop of Grandfolk.

entries.name: Ardryllus Sim'vara
entries.content: Ardryllus Sim'vara (576-818 AEKE), was a Froturnish general, one of the two consuls of Froturn between 809 and 818 alongside Ta'ael Myrth'nddare, a highly influental figure in Froturnish politics and considered one of the most pivotal figures of the decade preceding his death.

entries.name: Arnélia Gervése
entries.content: Arnélia Gervése is a 17-year old Human Cleric from Etrand. She has longer red hair and blue eyes.

entries.name: Arqun Valsavis
entries.content: Arqun Valsavis is a 34-year old Neressan Human Warrior.

entries.name: Ashrám Wegnard
entries.content: Ashrám Wegnard is a Lich Death Knight. His ultimate goal is to achieve godhood.

entries.name: Beoldwin Mairkel
entries.content: Beoldwin Mairkel (721794 AEKE) was an Etrandish Knight, former lover of King Bryant I of Etrand, later one of the main advisors - the main advisor, according to some - of King Cairbré I of Etrand. He was also the main censor during the reign of Cairbré, spearheading the infamous Cairbrean Censorship. The late Beoldwin is also known for being the father of Drugó Mairkel, the current Chancellor of Etrand.

entries.name: Bloody Thiedbold
entries.content: Bloody Thiedbold - also known as "The Blond Wolf of the Sea" or "The Dire Wolf of the Sea" - is an infamous Etrancoasti Pagan pirate, often considered the most dangerous of his kind. There is a very high bounty on his head, as he is hunted by both the earl and the Inquisition. While he is considered little better than scoundrel - strong and dangerous scoundrel, but still scoundrel - by his homeland's elite, a good deal of the peasantry is sympathetic to him and considers him their well-wisher.

entries.name: Bourn Garbald
entries.content: Bourn Garbald is a 45-year old Etrandish Human Knight, known for being a close friend to Stephánus Tavilrond and his late mentor Hlaford Paratus. He was also the apprentice of Julius William Etrix from 799 to 807.

entries.name: Brelon Tondbertling
entries.content:
Brelon Tondbertling (697-767 AEKE) was an Etrandish nobleman, son of Zylf Tondbertling, and one of the participants of the Etrandish Succession War of 718. He was pardoned for his participation in the civil war by King Bryant I of Etrand, and ended up as the Grand Count of Brevia, after all of his father's brothers were either dead or charged with high treason, with their children either being deemed too young to rule the county, or being in exile.

Brelon remained active in court politics well into the beginning of Cairbré-era, having left the royal court only after the king refused to marry his daughter.

entries.name: Cla'evar
entries.content: Clae'var is a High Elven Vampire Magician from Froturn. She has long red hair and red eyes, the latter of which is the result of her vampirism. Even though she looks 19 years old, she is actually 401 years old.

entries.name: Couroughis family
entries.content: The Couroughis family is a notable family in Talon. They claim to have very deep roots in Talon, claiming to be descendants of a yeoman bearing the same surname as them, the yeoman who led the effort to rebuild Talon two years after the Long Raid.

entries.name: Cradar the Once-Unclean
entries.content: Cradar the Once-Unclean a Human medicine-man and the most notable frequenter of the Purple Brother Brothel. As a man with much knowledge in alchemy, healing magic, medicine, surgery and disease-lore, he makes his money by actively preventing the fine ladies at the brothel - and their clients - from catching sexually-transmitted diseases, as well as using magic and/or alchemy to cure them if preventive measures fail. One might wonder why would a man with such skills would choose such a lowly establishment to cultivate his talents, instead of lending himself to hire for someone who is guaranteed to pay much more: Cradar is more than meets the eye and his dark and troubled past as a former Necromancer made him a pariah in the eyes of law-abiding polite society, making him an outlaw, a criminal whose very existence is a crime. Thankfully, he is not famous, very few know his name, and even fewer would recognize his face, thus, only a handful would be able to call him out for his past crimes in his face. Nevertheless, he keeps a low profile, living rather frugally.

entries.name: Crown Prince Bryant of Etrand
entries.content:
Crown Prince Bryant the Fair (777-809 AEKE) was the heir apparent of Etrand until his death in 809, eldest son of King Calhoun I of Etrand. Two weeks after his premature death, his father died of a broken heart, leaving Bryant's younger brother, Calhoun's second son Orlonius to inherit the throne.

Bryant is widely remembered as a virtuous man, a hero and defender of the faith.

entries.name: Crown Prince Markal of Etrand
entries.content: Crown Prince Markal is the current heir apparent in the Kingdom of Etrand. He has a younger sister, Princess Izaverra. Prince Markal has long brown hair and blue eyes.

entries.name: Cýr Cassian
entries.content:
Cýr Cassian is a representative of the Knights of the Blood Red Light in Tanqutařa / New Copperport. Operating under the facade of a virtuous knight and benefactor of the community (operating an orphanage, per his knightly order's policy), Cassian's true nature as a corrupt and malevolent force has not yet come to be public knowledge. His intricate web of deception involves the operation of an orphanage concealing a sinister child trafficking operation, with connections to the notorious Pepetoka gangster Nawqi Jaaba and the Zmogars.

His intricate scheme of corruption and cruelty has remained hidden from the public eye, but the day of reckoning may loom closer as the threads of his deception begin to unravel.

entries.name: Darléna Ellanva-Zarndél
entries.content: Darléna Ellanva-Zarndél is a High Elf Magician from Froturn. She has short brown hair, green eyes and large breasts. She is very tall.

entries.name: Drugó Mairkel
entries.content: Drugó Mairkel is an 67-years old Etrandish politician; son of the late Beoldwin Mairkel; the current Chancellor of Etrand; former advisor of the late King Calhoun I of Etrand; one of the advisors of the current King Orlónius I of Etrand. Some believe that he is to be credited for the relative stability Etrand has enjoyed ever since King Orlónius came to power - a king that listens to to Drugó's advices seems to be a king who brings stability to the realm.

entries.name: Elbek Hammerhand
entries.content: Elbek Hammerhand is a Dwarven Warrior.

entries.name: Elhiérus Ardacýn
entries.content: Elhiérus Ardácýn (122-595 AEKE) was a Froturnish scholar, composer, music theorist, philosopher and critic of culture and arts, and later of the Titanist religion itself.

entries.name: Elvavéna Aralíne
entries.content: Elvavéna Aralíne is a High Elven resident of Lynsaarne, a farmer and a novice magician. Born into a family of three sisters, Ethilla, Aralina, and Arathael, Elvavéna has also embraced motherhood, raising her son Thellis. While her nephew remains estranged, Elvavena's familial connections shape her journey. Elvavéna has long blonde hair, blue eyes and small breasts.

entries.name: Engmerk Hýrm
entries.content: Engmerk Hýrm (689-733 AEKE) was an Etrandish nobleman and one of the closest comrades of King Bryant I of Etrand - a member of his inner circle -, having supported him during the Etrandish Succession War of 718. Despite having shown loyalty to Bryant even before the latter's ascension to royalty, Engmerk inexplicably betrayed Bryant during Aederik's Revoultion, siding with the rebels against the royal authorities. For his treason, Engmerk was executed at the end of the war by his best friend Yosál Méró. Engmerk was also known for his controversial relationship with Lumina Tondbertling.

entries.name: Ermenerd Brynling
entries.content: Ermenerd Brynling is a 34-year old Etrandish aristocrat, and currently a steward serving under King Orlónius I of Etrand. He is a close associate of Crown Prince Markal of Etrand.

entries.name: Euphemy Sylvaine
entries.content: Euphemy Sylvaine is a Half-Elven Druid and Alchemist. She has long green hair (which she usually puts into twin braids), green eyes, large breasts and a short stature.

entries.name: Fathred the Great
entries.content: Fathred the Great was the very first ruler of a unified Etrand, reigning from 1138 BEKE until his death some time around 1110 BEKE. He is considered a national hero and the nation's founder by the people of Etrand, while he is viewed as little more than a barbarian overlord by the High Elves and the Wood Elves - as such, he is also known as "Fathred, Bane of the Knife-Ears".

entries.name: Fëanor Léralondë
entries.content: Fëanor Léralondë is a Dragoci Half-Orcish Half-Elven Ranger.

entries.name: Frythild Shairskwynn
entries.content: Frythild Shairskwynn (750-820 AEKE) was an Etrancoasti Bard and novelist. Even though he wrote poems, songs and novels alike, he is most famous for his novels, namely Sodobane - The Tears of Syrúna, Waterburcht Burning and Flowers of Titanius. He is considered one of the pinnacles of Etrancoasti language literature, although the values of his novels convey have aroused controversy.

entries.name: Gaius Frostang
entries.content: Gaius Frostang is a 56-year old Etrandish Human Knight and the current leader of the Knights of the Blood Red Light.

entries.name: Ghéri Myrnáld
entries.content: Ghéri Myrnáld (681-733 AEKE) was an Etrandish farmer, merchant and peasant rebellion leader, best known for his role in Aederik's Revoultion.

entries.name: Gnarog Dougfrál
entries.content: Gnarog Dougfrál is a Human Battlemage from Etrand, and the husband of Nemezish. He has long brown hair and green eyes. He is friends with Ladislaus Dominus, Stephánus Tavilrond, Morthen Orden'Áth Ildor and Nemezish.

entries.name: Green Sister
entries.content: Green Sister is a Winged Cobra. Her disguise is an illusion of a green-haired teenage human girl.

entries.name: Gregoreon Zachaxtrahy
entries.content: Gregoreon Zachaxtrahy is a 24-year old Etrandish Human Magician, who was raised by Gnomes. He has a highly eccentric sense of fashion: he wears his hair in dreadlocks and nearly consistently wears large glasses.

entries.name: Gzaxia Nolánó
entries.content: Gzaxia Nolánó is an Etrandish Half-Elf (Dark Elf from mother's side, Human from father's side) magician and scientist. The fact that she is also a vampire is unknown, since she is a magician who conducts dangerous experiments - some which may possibly slow down ageing or metabolism - she is not under scrutiny or suspicion, even though her apparent age should be 62 for a Half-Elf, or 40 for a Dark Elf. She has a son too, named Rael Nolánó. She has long red hair.

entries.name: Hairang the Corruptor
entries.content: Hairang the Corruptor (1316 BEKE - 259 AEKE) was a Lizardman Necromancer, later Demonic General. He was best known for being the mentor of Yenos the Dark.

entries.name: Hantilen Broyté Londers
entries.content:
Hantilen Broyté Londers (664-806 AEKE) - better known by his shorter name Hens Londers - born Guŕuq Brutti, was an Orcish-Etrandish cartographer, chronicler and historian.

He was described as a walking defiance to Orcish stereotypes - he was civilized, not aggressive at all, maybe even somewhat timid and shy. Due to his rather shy nature, he was unwilling to meet people personally, heavily preferring communicating via letters instead.

entries.name: Hardés Rózong
entries.content: Hardés Rózong (684-752 AEKE) was an Etrandish nobleman and one of the closest comrades of King Bryant I of Etrand - a member of his inner circle -, having supported him during the Etrandish Succession War of 718.

entries.name: Hastira Óseavirra
entries.content: Hastira Óseavirra, is an Etrandish High Elf Magician, who joined the Mages Guild of Grandfolk to delve into the arcane. In this prestigious institution, her charm made her a social presence. Yet, her haughty attitude displayed Elven supremacy, leading to bullying, especially towards Lotte Faróna, whom she mocked for assimilating into human culture. Hastira's interactions with peers exposed hypocrisy in her character. Despite projecting Elven supremacy, her romantic interests primarily involved Human men, contradicting her professed High Elven values.

entries.name: Héli Calbae
entries.content: Héli Calbae (759-829 AEKE) was an Etrandish Vampire Death Knight best known for partnership and association with Ria Baeni, as well as being involved in the murder of Hlaford Paratus and being killed by his apprentice Stephánus Tavilrond, just like her associate Baeni.

entries.name: Hió of Artaburro
entries.content: Hió is a Half-Elven member of the Etrandish royal court: was the wife of King Calhoun of Etrand and Queen Consort of Etrand between 789 and 809, making her the mother of the currently reigning King Orlónius I of Etrand. After the death of her husband, she became the Queen Mother, continuing to live in the royal palace. She has long white hair and blue eyes, and the appearance of a 31-year old woman, even though she is 87 years old.

entries.name: Hlaford Paratus
entries.content: Hlaford Paratus (794-829 AEKE) was an Etrandish Knight and the master of Stephánus Tavilrond.

entries.name: Hral the Hunter
entries.content: Hral the Hunter is a 32-year old Half-Orcish Warrior from Etrand.

entries.name: Ignátius the Necromancer
entries.content: Ignátius is a human Cryomancer-turned-Necromancer, who has managed to achieve immortality without becoming undead himself. He has long brown hair, a full beard and blue eyes.

entries.name: Ithric Drakrumhal
entries.content: Ithric Drakrumhal is Etrandish Half-Elf Ranger. His companion and best friend is Lumina Hwisberis. Due to his Elven heritage, he appears as a 21-year old man, despite being 38 years old. He has long black hair and blue eyes.

entries.name: Julius William Etrix
entries.content: Julius William Etrix (744-808 AEKE) was the leader of the Knights of the Blood Red Light between 785 and 808, the precedessor - and also former master - of the current leader Gaius Frostang.

entries.name: Kélen
entries.content: Kélen is a 36-year old Etrandish Human Assassin.

entries.name: Kerlon Tondbertling
entries.content: Kerlon Tondbertling (673-718 AEKE) was an Etrandish prince, younger brother of King Calder I of Etrand, and one of the participants of the Etrandish Succession War of 718 on the usurper/rebel side (together with his brothers Zylf and Symner). He was imprisoned after losing the Battle of Morshu's Mill, and subsequently executed for high treason after the end of the civil war. He was also the father of Lumina Tondbertling, who was most known for her controversial relationship with Engmerk Hýrm.

entries.name: Keshuver Seward
entries.content: Keshuver Seward (503-534 AEKE), also known by his nickname Keshú (Middle Etrandish: Keshú ; IPA: [kɛʃuː]), was an Etrandish Knight, best known as the first lover and murder victim of Ashrám Wegnard, immortalizing his name as a martyr.

entries.name: Khardung the Destroyer
entries.content: Khardung the Destroyer was a Lizardman Magician, later Necromancer, originally a member of the Mějaiyüt, later founding the Order of the Bone. Many believe that after his supposed death, he ascended to become a deity. He was born in 4021 BEKE and died at an unknown time after 3400 BEKE.

entries.name: King Bourn I of Etrand
entries.content: King Bourn I of Etrand (626-688 AEKE ) was the ruler of Etrand between 664 and 688 AEKE. He was considered the last "proper" King under the Tondbertid dynastiy, although some would say that the Tonodbertid dynasty's decline began under his reign, as there was quite a bit of dynastic infighting during his early reign.

entries.name: King Bryant I of Etrand
entries.content:
King Byrant I of Etrand - born Ladislaus Londbert - was the de facto ruler of Etrand between 718 and 744 AEKE, and founder of the Bryantid dynasty, even though he never identified as such, preferring to view his reign as the continuation of the Tondbertid dynasty's rule.
King Bryant was born in 687 AEKE. After studying at the royal academy, he rose through the ranks in the royal bureaucracy, but got into conflicts with King Calder I of Etrand, which resulted in his reassignment to the Dwarven lands. In 718, he became the leader of Queen Mythela's loyalists during the Etrandish Succession War of 718. After winning the war, he married Queen Mythela of Etrand and became the kingdom's de facto ruler.

entries.name: King Cael'mus of Froturn
entries.content: King Cael'mus the Lean (569-809 AEKE) - also known as Cael'mus the Impious - was the King of Froturn between 691 and 809 AEKE. His reign was characterized by an increase in royal authority at the expense of both the senate and various local governments, leading to accusation of tyranny. Quite controversially, the king also enacted a series of unofficial reforms regarding religious freedoms and authority that caused outrage among the native nobility and clergy, ultimately leading to the Froturnish Civil War.

entries.name: King Cairbré I of Etrand
entries.content: King Cairbré the Wise (723-789 AEKE) was the ruler of Etrand between 744 and 789. He is credited with the consolidation of the Bryantid dynasty's rule in Etrand - while his predecessor viewed his own rule as the continued of the Tondbertid dynasty's rule, Cairbré retconned his predecessor as the starter of a new dynasty: the Bryantid dynasty.

entries.name: King Calder I of Etrand
entries.content: King Calder the Unready (664-718 AEKE) was the ruler of Etrand between 688 and 718 AEKE, and the last ruling male member of the Tondbertid dynasty. He had three brothers: Kerlon Tondbertling, Zylf Tondbertling and Symner Tondbertling. He had only one child: Queen Mythela of Etrand.

entries.name: King Calhoun I of Etrand
entries.content: King Calhoun the Sad (748-809 AEKE) was the ruler of Etrand between 789 and 809.

entries.name: King Corlagon I of Etrand
entries.content: King Corlagon I (51 BEKE - 17 AEKE) was the ruler of Etrand between 0 AEKE and 17 AEKE. Corlagon is credited with being the founder of the Kingdom of Etrand, as well as the first king of the Corlagonid dynasty of Kings. He is venerated as a saint by the Church of Titanius.

entries.name: King Cuthbert I of Etrand
entries.content:
King Cuthbert I of Etrand (242-318 AEKE) was the ruler of Etrand between 275 and 318 AEKE. He was most remembered for his actions prior to his rulership - his actions during the Second Demonic Invasion and the The Long Raid. He is remembered as a highly skilled and talented general, a military genius. The 43 years he sent as a ruler are largely overshadowed by his actions in previous wars.

He was also known as the Steel Wolf, an epithet he won by rumours of him being "indestructible" and fearsome. While originally, it was a reference to his tendency to come out unscathed from all sorts of dangerous situations, and striking fear into the hearts of his enemies, by the time he was very old, it became a reference to his "refusal to die".

entries.name: King Ivahó of Froturn
entries.content: King Ivahó (28-years old, has long blonde hair) is the current reigning King of Froturn. De jure, he has been the ruler of Froturn ever since 809, but since he was underage when crowned, a regency council led by Consul Sim'vara and Ta'ael Myrth'nddare ruled in his stead until 818. Even though he is the reigning king now, both de jure and de facto, it is not known how much authority can he truly wield under the watchful influence of the clergy and nobility.

entries.name: King Orlónius I of Etrand
entries.content:
King Orlónius (47 years old, has long brown hair and full beard, blue eyes) is the current ruler of Etrand, reigning since the year 809 AEKE. Considered a military genius and a just monarch, opinion of him was not always as favourable, and even today, many dark corners of Grandfolk shelter whispers about his coming to power and the decline of morality within the Kingdom in the past 22 years. He is said to be especially unpopular abroad. Currently, he has a son named Markal and a daughter name Izaverra.

His main advisors are Drugó Mairkel and Theuderic Ragenald Merovéch.

entries.name: King Tondbert I of Etrand
entries.content: King Tondbert I the Pious (118-194 AEKE) was the ruler of Etrand between 146 and 182. Even though he wasn't technically the first monarch of the Tondbertid dynasty, the dynasty is named after him. Additionally, he was the only King of Etrand to date to abdicate the throne rather than die reigning, if we don't count Queen Mythela of Etrand, whose reign was complicated.

entries.name: Kymbern Londbert
entries.content: Kymbern Londbert (665-726 AEKE) or Kymbern of Myrrbaria was the Count of Myrrbaria and Head of House Londbert from 697 (the death of his father) to 721 (his abdication) and the father of King Bryant I of Etrand.

entries.name: Lachdanann An'Dubh
entries.content: Lachdanann An'Dubh is an Etrandish Warrior and the leader of the Black Eagle Company, a group of mercenaries. He is 27 years old, has long brown hair and blue eyes.

entries.name: Ladislaus Davró
entries.content: Ladislaus Davró (683-742) was an Etrandish nobleman and one of the closest comrades of King Bryant I of Etrand - a member of his inner circle -, having supported him during the Etrandish Succession War of 718. After King Bryant's ascension to kingship, Davró served as the king's Chancellor and Spymaster (only informally, as no such formal title exists) until his death. Davró's tenure was marred by his long-standing rivalry with the similarly scheming Sindmar Liúdolfinger (who competed with Davró for the role of Spymaster) and a lack of popularity and trust from the other members of Bryant's inner circle. Davró's power and influence led to fears, suspicions and speculations about his potential motives, but ultimately, he had no real ambitions beyond loyally serving Bryant as his Gray Eminence. Despite being distrusted by other members of the king's inner circle, Davró himself died defending the king from an assassination attempt.

entries.name: Ladislaus Dominus
entries.content: Ladislaus Dominus is a 22-year old Human mercenary Battlemage. He has short black hair and brown eyes, and is known as a womanizer. He is friends with Stephánus Tavilrond, Gnarog Dougfrál, Morthen Orden'Áth Ildor and Nemezish.

entries.name: Leugair Sárling
entries.content: Leugair Sárling (718-781 AEKE) was an Etrandish nobleman, gourmet and at a time one of the several crossdressing male lovers of King Bryant I of Etrand. Leugair's Rice Delight was named after him. Contrary to various speculations - due to his surname - he had no connection to the Shár Empire.

entries.name: Leyál Wýrm
entries.content: Leyál Wýrm (689-758 AEKE) was an Etrandish nobleman and one of the closest comrades of King Bryant I of Etrand - a member of his inner circle -, having supported him during the Etrandish Succession War of 718.

entries.name: Lilith
entries.content: Lilith, a demonic creation, shaped by her overlord Shamowel, usually assumes the appearance of a 15-year-old girl with long brown hair and blue eyes in a maid's dress. Despite her inherently evil nature, she displays complexity, harboring interests and a form of demonic love. Trained for ruthlessness, she's also playful and selectively protective. A skilled liar, she crafts oaths with exploitable loopholes for duty's sake. Despite her forgetfulness, demonic blood binds her to certain oaths. Socially needy, she relishes others' suffering but shows fanaticism if something valuable is at risk. Childish and clumsy in the mortal realm, she hides her above-average intelligence.

entries.name: Lotte Faróna
entries.content: Lotte Faróna is a High Elven resident of Lynsárne, and innkeeper, magician and the author of the book Inn-credible, as well as great-granddaughter of the famous hero Beravélus Faróna. She is the current owner of the the Faróna's Necklace. She has long blonde hair, blue eyes, a short stature and a flat chest, typically wearing orange clothes. She briefly studied at the Royal Academy of Grandfolk, where she was bullied by Hastira Óseavirra for  her flat chest and assimilation into human culture.

entries.name: Lumina Hwisberis
entries.content: Lumina Hwisberis is a 15-year old Etrancoastish Human thief, and additionally the best friend and companion of Ithric Drakrumhal. She has long blonde hair and blue eyes.

entries.name: Lumina Tondbertling
entries.content: Lumina Tondbertling (700-772 AEKE) was an Etrandish princess, daughter of Kerlon Tondbertling, an Etrandish prince who was executed for rebelling against the crown. She is most known for her controversial relationship with Engmerk Hýrm.

entries.name: Maraq saar-Wandi
entries.content: Maraq saar-Wandi was the founder of Wandism, a controversial tritheistic religion followed nearly exclusively by Qaemedi people.

entries.name: Márius Móga
entries.content: Márius Móga is an Etrandish Inquisitor. He is a 32-year old bald, muscular Human Male.

entries.name: May'diira Hun'ath
entries.content: May'diira Hun'ath 8-year old is a Dark Elven Female Necromancer.

entries.name: Mirabil
entries.content: Mirabil is a nature fairy.

entries.name: Morshu
entries.content:
Morshu (683-748 AEKE), also known as Morshu the Magnificent and Morshu the Merchant-King, hailed from Etrand and rose to wealth as a merchant, founding the Morshugger Dynasty. Born a peasant, he lost his livelihood in the Battle of Morshu's Mill. Compensation from King Bryant enabled him to restart as a merchant.

Facing financial struggles in Etrand, Morshu fled to Gabyr, where he thrived and financed a successful Eastern trading expedition. Returning to Etrand, he reconciled but maintained his trade empire in Gabyr. Leveraging his connection to Bryant, Morshu influenced royal decisions, notably in the Second Spice War, securing immense wealth.

Upon Bryant's death, Morshu settled in New Copperport, engaging in underworld dealings. He outlived Bryant by four years, succumbing to a heart attack. His descendants inherited his vast trade empire.

entries.name: Morthen Londbert
entries.content: Morthen Londbert (691-761 AEKE) or Morthen of Myrrbaria was the Count of Myrrbaria and Head of House Londbert from 721 (the abdication of his father) to 761 (his own death) and the younger brother of King Bryant I of Etrand. He was also the Marshal of Etrand from 722 until 752.

entries.name: Morthen Orden'Áth Ildor
entries.content: Morthen Orden'Áth Ildor - usually known just as Ildor - is a Human Ranger from Etrand. He has long blonde hair and green eyes. He is friends with Gnarog Dougfrál, Nemezish, Stephánus Tavilrond and Ladislaus Dominus.

entries.name: Muyian of Artaburro
entries.content: Muyian (725-789 AEKE) was the wife of King Cairbre I of Etrand and Queen Consort of Etrand between 746 and 789. She was a Half-Elf and the wife of King Cairbré I of Etrand.

entries.name: Nawqi Jaaba
entries.content: Nawqi Jaaba is a Pepetoka crime boss, the current leader of the Jaaba Crime Empire, the son and successor of the deceased Qrolba Jaaba. He loves underage human girls.

entries.name: Negbiarth Pheidoras
entries.content: Negbiarth Pheidoras (680-726) was an Etrandish celebrity, orator and writer. He was considered by most either a philosopher or a stand-up comedian or both, even though he always insisted that he was a scientist. He was a critic of magic, religion, feudalism and self-rule, for which he often clashed with authorities during the reign of King Calder I of Etrand, until King Bryant I of Etrand. Although he was considered little more than a joke during his life, after his suicide, his "fan-club" exploded until it was suppressed during the infamous Cairbrean Censorship.

entries.name: Nemezish
entries.content: Nemezish is a Human Battlemage from Etrand, and the wife of Gnarog Dougfrál. She has long white hair and blue eyes. He is friends with Ladislaus Dominus, Stephánus Tavilrond, Morthen Orden'Áth Ildor and Gnarog Dougfrál.

entries.name: Nilaradra Snécsír
entries.content: Nilaradra Snécsír also known as Nirara Neikishi is a High Elven Magician. She is a 10-year old girl with long blonde hair.

entries.name: Orikexir Spaendjekkel
entries.content: Orikexir Spaendjekkel is an Etrandish Dark Elven Bounty Hunter and Assassin. Due to his Elven heritage, he has the appearence of a 21-year old man in spite of being 54 years old.

entries.name: Phoenix Emperor
entries.content: The Phoenix Emperor (fl. 1125 BEKE) was a legendary individual - assumed to be more myth than reality by some skeptics - who is alleged to be the ancestor of the Emperors of Neressa via an unbroken bloodline, and is most famous for defeating the forces of Fathred's Confederation during Fathred's failed "Southern Campaign" in 1125 BEKE.

entries.name: Pirothea Nelvarryl
entries.content: Pirothea Nelvarryl is a Dark Elven prominent citizen of Etrand, businesswoman and magician, a retired politician and semi-retired crime boss. During the reign of King Bryant I of Etrand, Pirothea was a member of his inner circle -, having supported him during the Etrandish Succession War of 718. Due to her Elven heritage, she has the appearence of a 30-year old woman at the age of 146 years. She has long white hair, red eyes, blueish-gray skin, large breasts.

entries.name: Princess Gina of Artaburro
entries.content: Princess Gina or Jina of Artaburro is the current reigning Princess of Artaburro. She is the older sister of Queen Mother Hió of Etrand. Due to her Elven heritage, she has the appearence of a 32-year old woman at the age of 88. She has long red hair.

entries.name: Princess Hong Mei Ling of Shár
keys: princess hong mei ling of shár
Princess Hong Mei Ling of Shár
entries.content: Princess Hong Mei Ling is a Limjiang princess in the Shár Empire, older sister of the currently reigning Emperor Hong Tsai Kat. She is 19 years old, has long black hair, brown eyes and large breasts, usually wearing dark purple and red clothes and a tiara.
entries.comment: Princess Hong Mei Ling of Shár

entries.name: Qrolba Jaaba
entries.content: Qrolba Jaaba (698-804 AEKE) was an infamous Pepetoka crime boss, the founder of the Jaaba Crime Empire. A highly controversial figure, during the height of his criminal career, his power and influence that of actual heads of state, and the tentacles of his criminal empire reached all the way to the Principality of Gabyr, the Empire of Týrýng, the Shár Empire and the Kingdom of Etrand - he also had a great impact on the Spice Wars. Following his death, his empire was taken over by his son Nawqi Jaaba.

entries.name: Queen Anélia of Etrand
entries.content: Queen Anélia of Etrand (260-319 AEKE) - née Anélia Dracfolden - was the queen consort of Etrand between 277 and 318 AEKE, consort of King Cuthbert I of Etrand.

entries.name: Queen Cairi of Dragoc
entries.content: Queen Cairi, the current Queen of Dragoc, has long red hair, and the appearence of a 40-year old woman at the age of 251 due to her elven heritage. She faces challenges in advancing her agenda due to opposition from Etrand and Froturn. Accusations of affairs with kings Cael'mus and Bryant have made her a controversial figure. Widowed in 711 after King Miúrin's death, Cairi hasn't remarried and has no heir. If she dies or abdicates, her sister Soriania is likely to inherit the throne. Cairi's reign is marked by Wood Elven influence in foreign territories, but her attempts have faced obstacles since the late 8th century in Etrand and with the rise of King Ivahó in Froturn.

entries.name: Queen Imani of Ayube
entries.content: Queen Imani of Ayube is the current ruler of the Qaemedi city-state of Ayube and a devout follower of Jayism. She has long white hair in dreadlocks, large breasts and is a futanari.

entries.name: Queen Izaverra of Etrand
entries.content: Queen Izaverra born Izaverra Tondbertling- is the current queen consort of Etrand. She is a Tondbertling, making her the very first Tondbertling to be anywhere near the Etrandish throne since the death of Queen Mythela of Etrand.  She is 38 years old, has long red hair.

entries.name: Queen Lynasa of Etrand
entries.content: Queen Lynasa (635-701 AEKE) - born Lynasa Frithunathling  - was the queen consort of King Bourn I of Etrand, who ruled Etrand between 664 and 688 AEKE. She was born in Etrancoast, and was the daughter of Earl Osnoth of Etrancoast, and the younger sister of Earl Shiwad of Etrancoast.

entries.name: Queen Mythela of Etrand
entries.content: Queen Mythela I of Etrand, was the last Tondbertid ruler of Etrand, having ruled de jure from 718 to 744 AEKE, reigning as queen regnant briefly in 718 (before her husband, King Bryant I of Etrand took control) and 744 (after Bryant died), being a de facto queen consort in the time between. She was the daughter of King Calder I of Etrand. She was the only ruler of Etrand - other than King Tondbert I of Etrand - to abdicate the throne rather than die reigning.

entries.name: Queen Salvia of Froturn
entries.content: Queen Salvia the Great (1392-1106 BEKE) or Tsëlwia was the first ruler of Froturn, ruling it from approximately ~1300 BEKE to 1106 BEKE.

entries.name: Queen Sellin Marand
entries.content:
Sellin Marand (378-473 AEKE), born Seléna Zathýr Merandi, was the first and only Queen of the Dark Elves, born a High Elven Magician before turning to the Dark Arts and being one of those who were exiled for that act.

Sellin was considered a charismatic leader during her life, records about her describe her as a charitable and sociable person with a firm personality, someone who - despite having quite a bit of beauty - relied on her sharp tongue to win debates.

entries.name: Rael Nolánó
entries.content: Rael Nolánó is an Etrandish Battlemage, and the oldest son of Gzaxia Nolánó. Due to a combination of his elven heritage and vampirism, he has the appearence of a 18-year old man at the age of 102 - he also has long white hair and red eyes. He is a very multilingual character - while his native tongue is Etrandish, he is also fluent at the Dark Elven, Despotanmagi, High Elven, Wood Elven and the Dwarven languages too. Inheriting his mother's freedom-loving nature, he too walks the earth, getting to know new people and things, usually running away before the people can spot him. His looks often cause fear among ordinary people, and he is well-aware. He still doesn't wish to look any different, as he is proud of what he is. He usually wears heavy armour, a cape and his main companion is a claymore. He earns his daily coin by hunting monsters and collecting bounty for them. To him, only two types exist: monsters and not-monsters. Even those who call themselves humans can easily fall into the first category.

entries.name: Rath Varss
entries.content: Rath Varss is an Etrandish Inquisitor. He is a 26-year old bald and muscular Human Male.

entries.name: Reyanna Cradling
entries.content: Reyanna Cradling (698-765 AEKE) was an Etrandish noblewoman and wife of Yosál Méró.

entries.name: Reyanna Rýger
entries.content: Reyanna Rýger, origianlly born as Elna is a Crainer Warrior from Etrand. She is 21 years old, has long blonde hair.

entries.name: Ria Baeni
entries.content: Ria Baeni (721-829 AEKE) was an Etrandish Vampire Necromancer best known for the murder of Hlaford Paratus and being killed by his apprentice Stephánus Tavilrond. It is said that Ria has terrorized the alleys of Grandfolk and the Etrandish countryside during her prime, and has built up a criminal network that fell apart after her death.

entries.name: Scatama Salorium
entries.content: Scatama Salorium (born 771 AEKE), also known by his nickname Saló is a Lizardman Shaman.

entries.name: Sepha Faróna
entries.content: Sepha Faróna (717-789 AEKE) née Haessinddare - was a High Elven resident of Lynsárne, and magician, mother of Lotte Faróna and the previous owner of the Faróna's Necklace. She was killed by an agent of Ashrám Wegnard.

entries.name: Sharog Shnaglurtz
entries.content:
Sharog Shnaglurtz, a 31-year-old Half-Orcish Warrior and ex-pirate, is Sinteris Carressa's loyal bodyguard. Born from a non-consensual union between a human and an orc, Sharog faced abandonment by her mother. Saved by orcs who identified her lineage, she endured her father's disdain, pushing her towards a more masculine identity. As an adult, she led raids on the Empire of Neressa and later became a notorious pirate captain.
Infamous for rumored atrocities, Sharog maintained a methodical approach with a semblance of a moral compass. Betrayed and imprisoned, she found redemption when saved by an angelic being, incurring a life debt to Cinteris Shea'darra. Loyalty to Sinteris overrides any moral conflicts, despite perceiving her as naive. Unconcerned with societal views, Sharog's dedication to guarding Sinteris is unwavering, even if they seldom appear together publicly.

entries.name: Sindmar Liúdolfinger
entries.content: Sindmar Liúdolfinger (688-749 AEKE) was an Etrancoasti nobleman's bastard (later legitimized nobleman) and one of the closest comrades of King Bryant I of Etrand - a member of his inner circle -, having supported him during the Etrandish Succession War of 718. After King Bryant's ascension to kingship, Liúdolfinger served as the King's Steward and competed with Ladislaus Davró for the role of Spymaster (which he acquired after Davró's death). His scheming nature put him at odds with other members of the royal court, especially the aforementioned Ladislaus Davró, with whom Sindmar had a lasting rivalry.

entries.name: Sinteris Carressa
entries.content: Sinteris Carressa is an Etrandish Magician. Her bodyguard and main companion is Sharog Shnaglurtz. Sinteris Carressa is a 24-year old woman with long blonde hair and brown eyes. Her birth name was Cinteris Shea'darra. Raised by a influential father devoted to the Church of Titanius, she initially followed her father's wishes but grew disillusioned with the church's atrocities. Forced into marriage by her father, she endured an abusive husband while secretly helping the common folk and criticizing the church. Witnessing an injustice, she intervened, cutting her husband's hand and escaping persecution. Captured by the Inquisition, she unexpectedly found freedom, and Sharog, the half-orc she saved, became her companion. They sought the Order of the Eternal Crystal Flower, where Sinteris became an apprentice. Despite Inquisition attacks, they continue their journey, aiming to uphold goodness.

entries.name: Stephánus Tavilrond
entries.content: Stephánus Tavilrond a 22-year old Human Knight from Grandfolk. He was born an orphan. He has long brown hair and azure-blue eyes. He is friends with Bourn Garbald, Ladislaus Dominus, Gnarog Dougfrál, Morthen Orden'Áth Ildor and Nemezish.

entries.name: Swidhelm Folkling
entries.content: Swidhelm Folkling (65-183 AEKE) was the first publicly known Vampire, one of the two founding fathers of the Republic of Keldorn (the other being Yenos the Dark, his mentor), and a key figure in Dead Man's Rise.

entries.name: Symner Tondbertling
entries.content: Symner Tondbertling (675-718 AEKE) was an Etrandish prince, younger brother of King Calder I of Etrand, and one of the participants of the Etrandish Succession War of 718 on the usurper/rebel side (together with his brothers Kerlon and Zylf).

entries.name: Ta'ael Myrth'nddare
entries.content: Ta'ael Myrth'nddare is a High Elven magician, former politician, former advisor to King Cael'mus of Froturn, one of the two consuls of Froturn (the other being Ardryllus Sim'vara) between 809 and 818. Despite having retired from politics for good, Ta'ael is viewed as one of the most influential figures of the century, playing a pivotal role in the history of Froturn before 818. She has long white hair and blue eyes. Due to her elven heritage, she has the appearence of a 31-year old woman at the age of 161 years.

entries.name: Tela’sildë Sarangerel
entries.content: Tela’sildë Sarangerel is a Dragon Magician. She 961 years old, but lives forever, which is one of the perks of being a Golden Dragon. She usually takes on the shape of a young human girl with white hair and blue eyes when deciding to intermingle with mortals.

entries.name: Tepirm Quatl
entries.content: Tepirm Quatl is a Lizardman Warrior-Thief.

entries.name: Ther'rah Alean'athem
entries.content: Ther'rah Alean'athem is a Dragon Necromancer. He is a black dragon who lives forever - nevertheless, when he intermingles with mortals, he takes on the form of an elf male. While evil, he is primarily motivated by a desire to resurrect his dead lover.

entries.name: The Tormentor
entries.content: The Tormentor, also known as Dermaglen in his human life, is a Vampire Death Knight with a bald appearance in his 30s. His origins are mysterious, and little is known about his past as Dermaglen, a once honorable knight consumed by obsession for a neglectful woman. Seeking a solution, he turned to Ashrám Wegnard, becoming a minion to create a perfect replica of his beloved. Despite the replica, he remains tormented by past pain, serving Ashrám loyally but harboring a burning desire for revenge. As a mentor under Ashrám, he is known as "the Tormentor," cruelly rooting out weakness among Cult Initiates aspiring to be Death Knights. Refusing to acknowledge his old name, "Dermaglen", he only identifies as "the Tormentor," claiming, "Dermaglen is dead. I killed him. Now only the Tormentor remains."

entries.name: Theuderic Ragenald Merovéch
entries.content: Theuderic Ragenald Merovéch is a 62-years old Etrandish former Inquisitor, and the current Spymaster of King Orlonius I of Etrand. He is a strong proponent of censorship and the Inquisition and believes that too much intellectual freedom can destabilize Etrand and weaken the government. He is also known for favouring a strong centralized government like that of Froturn over the current decentralized feudal system that Etrand has.

entries.name: Tiamat
entries.content: Tiamat is a Dragon adventurer. When intermingling with mortals, she takes on the shape of a young woman with short blue hair.

entries.name: Toma Dimple
entries.content: Toma Dimple is an Etrandish-born Halfling Magician, the leader of the Community of Antanath, and an important figure in the movement to revive Halfling Paganism. As a halfling, he has the appearence of a 44-year old man at the age of 75.

entries.name: Vaclus Helviatha
entries.content:
Vaclus Helviatha (35-248 AEKE) was a Froturnish general, later consul and king consort, de facto military dictator.

He is most well remembered for being a general in the Froturnish army during the Three Kings' War, launching a coup and overthrowing the Froturnish government during the Froturnish Civil War of 108-109. After winning the civil war, he deposed the reigning King Caelferus and pressured his daughter Ypsela to marry him. In the aftermath of the civil war - until his assassination in 248 - he was officially consul and de jure king consort to queen regnant Ypsela, while in the reality was the complete opposite, with Vaclus Helviatha ruling as a de facto military dictator till his assassination.

entries.name: Válistus Culiphae
entries.content: Válistus Culiphae, is a Froturnish nobleman, former general, and politician, the current military consul of Froturn, and one of the advisors of King Ivahó of Froturn. He was also known as being one of the main rivals of Ardryllus Sim'vara, having fought against him during the Froturnish Civil War, including in the Battle of Ancestors Field. He is also known for having played a part in orchestrating the coup against Sim'vara in 818. Válistus has long blonde hair, and due to his elven heritage, he has the appearence of a 32-year old man at the age of 158 years.

entries.name: Varsu Haliux
entries.content: Varsu Haliux, originally called Belihior, is an Etrandish Half-Elf Werewolf ex-Knight, currently a Death Knight in Keldorn. He has long white hair and looks like a 20-year old man, even though his actual age is 131 years.

entries.name: Vidiorta Amard
entries.content: Vidiorta Amard is an Etrandish Werewolf Warrior. He has black hair and a mustache, and usually wears a clock and covers his face. Due to his werewolf condition - which causes him to be undead and stops his ageing - he has the appearence of a 19-year old man despite being 46 years old.

entries.name: Willem Snebdjeli
entries.content: Willem Snebdjeli (407-475 AEKE) was an Etrancoasti nobleman and admiral, active during the First Cymbairan War.

entries.name: Yenos the Dark
entries.content: Yenos the Dark (48-183 AEKE) was the first publicly known Necromancer since the fall of the Ancient Lizardman Empire, one of the two founding fathers of the Republic of Keldorn (the other being Swidhelm Folkling, his first apprentice), and a key figure in Dead Man's Rise.

entries.name: Yosál Méró
entries.content: Yosál Méró (689-754 AEKE) was an Etrandish nobleman and one of the closest comrades of King Bryant I of Etrand - a member of his inner circle -, having supported him during the Etrandish Succession War of 718. Loyal to Bryant to the very end, Yosál's loyalty to the king was tested when his best friend and honorary brother Engmerk Hýrm betrayed the king during Aederik's Revoultion - Yosál in the end remained unflinchingly loyal to the king, and was in fact the one who execute his own best friend for the crime of treason.

entries.name: Ypsel
entries.content: Ypsel is a High Elven Warrior from Froturn. Due to her Elven heritage, she has the appearence of a 23-years old woman despite being 73 years old, she also has long brown hair, brown eyes, a gracile and slender figure. Ypsel, born in Yanus, didn't meet her family's shining expectations due to a lack of magical affinity. Uninterested in socializing, she favored swords over elves' traditional archery. Labeled the black sheep, she was expelled at the age of 30. Ypsel embraced her passion for sword fighting, surviving by accepting jobs. After thwarting cutthroats, she became a wandering mercenary, known for her skills but oblivious to the passing decades. Behind her cold exterior lies a simple, easily influenced mind.

entries.name: Y'rein
entries.content: Y'rein is a High Elven Magician. She has long white hair and the appearence of a 34-years old woman in spite of being 178 years old, due to her elven heritage. Y'rein, defied tradition by leaving her home at two years old, guided by a deceptive mage who claimed she had a prophesized role. Persuading her reluctant parents, the mage, skilled in forbidden arts, subtly influenced her education in the Mages Guild. He aimed for an apprentice with forbidden knowledge. Eventually, he took her on a journey, driven by the allure of eternal life. However, the mage was defeated in his quest for immortality, leaving behind Y'rein, a young Elf of thirty. She returned to the Mages Guild, mastering both legitimate and illegitimate crafts. Seeking independence, she ventured into the world, with the wisdom of long years but struggles with social connections, unlike her master.

entries.name: Zylf Tondbertling
entries.content: Zylf Tondbertling (677-718 AEKE) was an Etrandish prince, younger brother of King Calder I of Etrand, and one of the participants of the Etrandish Succession War of 718 on the usurper/rebel side (together with his brothers Kerlon and Symner). He was also the father of Brelon of Brevia. He was killed by his own men during the Battle of Morshu's Mill, after he ordered them to assassinate his brother Kerlon.

entries.name: BEKE
entries.content: BEKE stands for "Before the foundation of the Kingdom of Etrand".

entries.name: AEKE
entries.content: AEKE stands for "After the foundation of the Kingdom of Etrand".

entries.name: Fall of Qaem
entries.content:
The Fall of Qaem is a semi-historical event that happened some time around 200 BEKE, involving the fall of the Kingdom of Qaem and the destruction of its capital city Qaem at the hands of the Shíd during the Great Shíd Migration. 
There are different interpretations to the legend of Qaem, but the gist of the story is the following: the Shíd were besieging the ancient city of Qaem, and offered to spare the city and its inhabitants in exchange for Queen Jaya of Qaem marrying the Shíd leader Ndaalats. Queen Jaya refused, and instead had a relationship with the white-skinned Ledises - however, the high priest Ngushamun supported the idea of Jaya marrying Ndaalats, so he launched a coup, which was suppressed. The Shíd eventually broke through the defenses, Ledises sacrificed his life to delay the invaders, while Queen Jaya fled with the civilians.

entries.name: Demonic Invasions of Artograch
entries.content:
The Demonic invasions of Artograch were two military invasions (First Demonic Invasion in 251-253 AEKE, Second Demonic Invasion in 257-263) and attempts at colonization of Artograch by Demonic forces from Nortiimus. During both events, Demons from Nortiimus opened massive portals into Artograch and used their armies with the intent to conquer land, capture and enslave civilians and loot goods.

Even though both invasions got repelled, the Demonic invasions have left a major scar on Artograch that the continent's peoples would not recover from for at least a century. The consequences of the event still echo to this day. Among other things, the demonic invasions led to the foundation of the Alliance for the Light.

entries.name: Etrandish Succession War of 718
entries.content: The Etrandish Succession War of 718 - also known as the Brynatid Succession War, Tondbertid Civil War or Tondbertid Succession Crisis- was a civil war in the Kingdom of Etrand following the death of King Calder I of Etrand. Even though the conflict was won by Mythela, the legitimate heir, daughter of King Calder, her victory ultimately led to the downfall of the Tondbertids, as her husband King Bryant and his descendants ended up founding the new Bryantid dynasty.

entries.name: Bryantid dynasty
entries.content: The Bryantid dynasty - also known as Bryantling - has been the ruling family of the Kingdom of Etrand since 718 AEKE (unofficially) or 744 (officially), named after King Bryant I of Etrand.

entries.name: Tondbertid dynasty
entries.content: The Tondbertid dynasty - also known as Tondbertling - was the ruling family of Etrand between 145 and 718 AEKE - ruling Etrand for 69% of its history -, although the house's official deposition happened only in 744. Even though the Tondbertids no longer hold the royal title of Etrand, they continue to be a powerful noble family that still holds considerable amount of influence and prestige even to this day.

entries.name: House Londbert
entries.content: The House of Londbert  is a well-known but otherwise minor noble family in Etrand. They used to be one of the major noble houses of Etrand, but now they are a minor player. Throughout the family's history, many of the less talented heads of the family have managed to gradually gamble away much of the family's lands, both figuratively and literally, until they had no more land to gamble away, until they were stuck with just one small county - the County of Myrrbaria.

entries.name: Aederik's Revoultion
entries.content: Aederik's Rebellion, also known as the False King's War or Rape War, occurred during King Bryant I's reign in the Kingdom of Etrand. In 733, Aederik claimed to be King Calder's lost son, exploiting discontent fueled by a drought and anti-rapeseed laws. Peasants, led by Aederik and financed by Ghéri Myrnáld, revolted against King Bryant. Initially successful, Aederik's forces faced defeat at Mitrid Plains. Engmerk Hýrm, a loyal nobleman, inexplicably joined the rebels. The rebellion ended with Aederik's disappearance, Myrnáld's execution, and Hýrm's betrayal leading to his execution by Yosál Méró.

entries.name: Lumina Tondbertling & Engmerk Hýrm
entries.content: The nature of Lumina's relationship with Engmerk is shrouded in mystery and ambiguity, with historians still undecided just how consensual it really was: some claim that Engmerk easily seduced the young and naive Lumina, who willingly entered a sexual relationship with him, possibly out of the naive hope that it would earn her father Kerlon clemency. Others paint a far darker picture of their relationship, claiming that Engmerk violently kidnapped and raped her, evidenced by his own recorded words "I took her with my authority, and by violence 😼". A third group claims, that the relationship was consensual, and Lumina only began to (falsely) accuse Engmerk of rape after she became pregnant with his bastard son, or after her father Kerlon was executed for high treason in the aftermath of the succession crisis.

entries.name: Gray Mountains
entries.content: The Gray Mountains are a mountain range located within the center of Continental Artograch. Most of the mountain range is part of the Empire of Neressa.

entries.name: Magic Nexus
entries.content: A Magic Nexus - also called Nexus of Magic, Mana Nexus, "Window to Akasha" or simply "tear" - is a location characterized by heavy concentration of magic and various other attributes. Magic Nexuses are defined by a high concentration of Raw Mana, posing risks akin to radiation. Non-sentient animals instinctively avoid these areas. While harmful to most life, creatures like Mana Jelly thrive by converting raw mana faster than mortals. Swampy Magic Nexuses teem with Mana Jelly, while those underground, especially in mountains, contain Mana Crystals. They are dubbed "Windows to Akasha" or "tears" due to their perceived link between the mortal world and Akasha. Mortals aspiring to deity favor these locations for ascension rituals. Some view them as mystical "tears" or "holes" in the wall separating Akasha from the mortal world. Magic Nexuses, besides their mystical properties, are vital sources of power housing artifacts and magic sources. Their origin remains unknown; consensus suggests they can't be intentionally created by mortals, only through natural processes, divine intervention, or extraordinary events like large battles involving numerous spellcasters.

entries.name: Akasha
entries.content:
Akasha is the name given to the cosmic energy field that is used as the source of all magic, as well as the home of all deities. This energy field exists separate from the mortal world, without form or physics, an infinite ocean of energy. This place connects the consciousnesses and subconsciousnesses of all living creatures through the mana, or life energy, they contain. The gods reside in this dimension, they are powerful entities whose power is given by the believers. By harnessing the energies of Akasha, which requires a conduit - either the spellcaster's own body in case of Arcane Magic, or a deity in case of Clerical Magic - those in the mortal world can use it to weave their own will into magic spells, through which they can create or destroy.

There exists so called "Windows to Akasha" or "tears in reality" scattered throughout the world of Artograch, where the boundaries between Akasha and the mortal world are said to be at their thinnest.

entries.name: Mana
entries.content: Mana is a mystical substance that flows within the bloodstream of living beings (and seeps through the bones of certain undead beings) and holds a central role in the realm of magic. This ethereal essence is intimately connected to the casting of spells, as it is consumed and depleted during magical incantations (when using a conduit - whether one's own body or a deity's aid - to connect to Akasha), only to replenish and regenerate when spellcasters find respite in rest. Not all mana is created equal. Among other things, mana exists in two variants: raw mana and usable mana. Raw mana exists primarily in a gaseous form and, beyond a critical quantity or concentration (very are outside of Magic Nexuses), can expose organic life to perils similar to radiation. On the other hand, usable mana exists in a liquid form, or when compressed and condensed, it takes a solid state.

entries.name: Tanqutařa
entries.content: Tanqutařa, also known as New Copperport or Hyld Copperport is a city within the Reyang Peninsula, nominally an independent city-state, but in reality a Gabyrian colony ever since the Second Spice War. It is populated by a mixture of Pepetoka and Humans, with tensions brewing between the two groups.

entries.name: Crainers
entries.content:
Crainers, a semi-nomadic militarized subculture or ethnic group from Craina (Southeastern Etrand), mainly consist of Humans but also include Half-Orcs, Half-Elves, and Lizardmen. Despite nominal suzerainty to the Kingdom of Etrand, they reside in the wild and ungovernable southern boundaries called Craina. Facing frequent Orcish raids, Crainers operate with de facto autonomy, avoiding feudal obligations in exchange for serving as border guards and irregular cavalry.

While skilled warriors, Crainers have a reputation for disregarding laws, often turning into brigands off-duty and engaging in unsanctioned raids that provoke both Orcs and royal authorities. In the Earldom of Etrancoast, the notorious Royal Hounds, predominantly composed of Crainers, have terrorized dissident peasantry, earning Crainers a negative reputation since the Viceroyalty of Etrancoast. The Royal Hounds' brutal actions during the suppression of Rikwi's Pagan Rebellion have turned the term "crainer" into a swearword in the Etrancoasti language, used as a threat by mothers to discipline misbehaving children.
